title: The Dog and the Shadow: exercises
subtitle: Five exercises on the text
label: Exercises
review: Written by Claude from the lesson text. Check the English and the answers before using it with learners.

items.q: The dog found a big bone.
The dog wanted to find a busy place to eat.
The bridge over the stream was made of stone.
The other dog in the water was the dog's own reflection.
The dog's bone fell into the stream when he barked.
At the end, the dog got the other dog's bone.
How did the dog carry the bone?
items.why: “The dog picked up the bone in his mouth and trotted happily away.”

items.q: What did the dog see when he looked down into the water?
items.why: “There, in the water, he saw another dog!”

items.q: What did the dog think about the bone in the water?
items.why: "That bone looks bigger than mine!" he thought.

items.q: What happened to the dog's bone after it fell?
items.why: “The dog watched sadly as the bone sank beneath the water.”

items.q: What is the moral of the story?
options: Be happy with what you have
items.why: “Moral: Be happy with what you have.”

blocks.title: 4. Open questions
blocks.note: These questions are open. Talk about your answers with your teacher or a classmate.

items.q: Without looking at the text, sum it up in three sentences.
items.model: A hungry dog was carrying a big bone across a bridge. He saw his reflection in the water and thought it was another dog with a bigger bone. He barked at it, and his own bone fell into the stream.

items.q: What did the dog see in the water? What was it really?
items.model: He saw another dog with a bone in his mouth. It was really his own reflection.

items.q: Why did the dog open his mouth?
items.model: He wanted to bark at the other dog, because he wanted that bone too.

items.q: What did the dog understand at the end?
items.model: He understood his foolish mistake: he had lost his own bone because he wanted another.

items.q: Have you ever wanted something that someone else had? What happened?

blocks.title: 5. Put in order
blocks.intro: Put the events in the order of the story.
items: The dog found a big bone
The dog crossed a wooden bridge
The dog saw his reflection in the water
The dog barked at the other dog
The bone sank beneath the water
